960: In thirty years watching this lobby I never saw a guest so proud of doing nothing wrong.
961: They tipped me to stop watching them, which is exactly when I started watching them.
962: Every hotel detective learns a face. Theirs I learned in a second and lost in one blink.
963: They asked which cameras still worked, smiled at each one, and posed for it.
964: I follow the quiet guests. This one wanted to be followed and complained I was too slow.
965: The register said one night. The bill said a fortune. The room said they were never really there.
966: They wore dark glasses at the front desk at midnight and called it being discreet.
967: I have caught many guests sneaking out. Never one who checked out loudly and vanished quietly.
968: They gave three different names and were offended I only wrote down two.
969: Most guests hide from the house detective. This one asked me for an autograph first.
970: They asked to have every safe in the hotel opened 'for inspection' and inspected the contents fondly.
971: I size up every guest at the door in one glance. This one earned a second glance, and used it to leave.
972: They demanded the best room, refused it, then paid double for the trouble of refusing.
973: A guest that memorable should stay a while. Ours checked out before I finished writing the name.
974: They asked me the fastest way out of every exit and thanked me like I had given a gift.
975: In my logbook I write 'suspicious.' For this guest I ran out of room in the margin.
976: They left the room spotless, the safe empty, and a mint on the pillow for themselves.
977: I trailed them past the fountain; they stopped to admire their reflection and slipped away.
978: Every alarm they set off, they bowed to. I have never seen a guest enjoy trouble so much.
979: They checked in with ten trunks and out with eleven, and I only ever carried the ten.
980: I told them to step back from the glass. They stepped closer and thanked me for the tour.
981: They admired one painting so long I thought they lived here. This morning it is the one missing.
982: My whole job is keeping hands off the art. Theirs applauded the art instead, which felt worse.
983: They asked which piece the museum loved most, then guarded it far more jealously than I ever had.
984: I have guarded this hall for years. One guest leaned in, and one treasure leaned out.
985: They complimented my uniform, my post, and my sharp eyes, then walked right past all three.
986: They stood on the rope line and told me it was there to protect them from the art.
987: I blinked once at my station. The frame is still here; the painting inside it is not.
988: They asked if the alarms were for the art or for the visitors, and smiled at both answers.
989: Most people admire the statues. This one measured them with their eyes.
990: They leaned so close their nose nearly signed the canvas. Now the canvas is elsewhere.
991: They told me a real guard would let them touch just one. I said no. It is gone anyway.
992: They fed the whole room compliments and left with the only piece worth stealing.
993: I watched the crowd. The crowd watched them. They watched only the priceless one.
994: They asked me to guard their coat while they got 'a closer look.' I never saw either again.
995: They saluted every guard in the hall as if we were the exhibit.
996: For one grand hour they were the best-behaved guest here. The hour the vault emptied.
997: They asked me to brighten one painting 'so it could truly shine.' Now the brightest thing there is the empty wall.
998: I keep the treasures safe from grabbing hands. Nobody warned me about admiring ones.
999: They stood at attention beside me for a photograph, then robbed the room I was guarding.
